mapping_rule_applied: The mapping rule the ais terms record quotes (fixtures/ais/spec/ais_terms.json): a standard or data service the publisher states is a free public offering of a public body -> PUBLIC_GOVERNMENT; an open licence released by its author -> OPEN. Applied: Frost is the free data API of the Norwegian Meteorological Institute, a government agency, whose licensing page names the Norwegian Licence for Open Government Data (NLOD) and Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International and asks for a credit. Two readings fit (both licences are open, so OPEN is defensible); the government-publisher reading is the one this package's precedents for agency data services take (ndbc_stdmet, coops_csv, airnow_hourly), and it is the one recorded. Both readings are stated here so a later ruling can take the other without re-reading the pages.
not_committed: This record is a reading of the publisher's pages, not an acquisition and not a pin: no document was downloaded into this repository, no hash of any page is claimed, and no clause is transcribed beyond the quoted sentences below. It states no permission: where a page is silent, the record says so rather than inferring a grant. It does not claim the pages still read this way after read_at; a later reading is a later record beside this one. A Frost response's own `license` field is carried verbatim by the adapter and may name another edition (CC BY 3.0 NO was observed); reconciling the response's statement with the licensing page is the consumer's, and this record does not do it.
